reviewer_role: GLOBAL-P0 R3 PROMOTION CONTROL-COMPATIBILITY INDEPENDENT REVIEWER

critical_findings.title: Historical revision allowlist is not executable provenance-only authorization
critical_findings.detail: evaluate_passport_architecture_compatibility() decides a mismatched passport compatible using only the enabled policy mode, the policy-selected registry field, and membership of the passport architecture revision in that program entry's allowlist. audit_program() then removes ARCHITECTURE_REVISION_MISMATCH and recomputes health. No executable predicate binds the exception to an already-historical/frozen passport identity or rejects a newly created/refreshed post-promotion runtime frontier. Therefore adding or retaining the historical allowlist on a future runtime registry entry is sufficient to suppress the architecture mismatch when all other findings are clean. The textual transition rules FROZEN_R2_EVIDENCE_GRANDFATHERED, NEW_RUNTIME_AFTER_PROMOTION_USES_R3 and STALE_AUTHORIZATION_FAILS_CLOSED are not consumed by this compatibility path.

counterexample.effect: ARCHITECTURE_REVISION_MISMATCH is removed; no separate compatibility-path rule rejects the new/refreshed R2 runtime frontier

critical_findings.title: Missing central_registry_field is not fail-closed
critical_findings.detail: When passport_architecture_compatibility.mode is enabled but central_registry_field is absent, the implementation silently substitutes historical_passport_architecture_revisions via _DEFAULT_REGISTRY_FIELD. A malformed/incomplete compatibility policy can therefore still authorize a historical mismatch instead of failing closed. The current policy file contains the correct field, but the implementation contract is weaker than the required fail-closed semantics.

critical_findings.title: Regression suite does not prove provenance-only denial for new runtime
critical_findings.detail: The focused tests prove exact-match, disabled policy, exact allowlist, unlisted revision, malformed allowlist type, health preservation, the six live R2 passports in synthetic R3, and G allowlist removal. They do not include the critical negative case where a new/refreshed post-promotion runtime frontier carries R2 plus an allowlist and must remain RED, nor the missing-central_registry_field fail-closed case.

required_fixes.requirement: Make provenance-only eligibility executable and independent of role/status string heuristics. A historical architecture allowlist must not, by itself, be sufficient to suppress ARCHITECTURE_REVISION_MISMATCH for a new or refreshed post-promotion frontier. Bind compatibility to an explicit main-owned historical passport identity captured at the promotion boundary (at minimum exact program, branch/passport identity, historical architecture revision, and immutable/pinned historical head or equivalent durable provenance identity), and fail closed when that identity no longer matches. A fresh runtime frontier must require the canonical architecture revision even if an old allowlist is accidentally copied or retained.

Require passport_architecture_compatibility.central_registry_field to be present and exactly equal historical_passport_architecture_revisions when compatibility mode is enabled. Remove the permissive fallback for an omitted field; missing, empty, or different field names must fail closed for mismatched revisions.

Add regression tests proving: (a) a newly created/refreshed post-promotion runtime frontier on R2 remains RED even when its program entry contains the R2 historical allowlist; (b) copying/retaining a historical allowlist onto a different/new passport identity cannot suppress ARCHITECTURE_REVISION_MISMATCH; (c) missing central_registry_field with mode enabled fails closed; and (d) the existing six historical R2 passport synthetic-R3 compatibility cases still pass. Rerun Project Control on the fixed implementation and lifecycle head and attach actual artifacts.
